projectMove.title: Site security: the first weekly sweep runs Tuesday
projectMove.body: The new weekly bug and exploit sweep makes its first pass this Tuesday around 10 AM, with Ram and Miyuki checking every site for booking-system weak spots, exposed private information, and broken links. Nothing goes live from it without your approval; any fix is prepared as a draft, and you will only hear about real findings, each with a simple yes or no decision.

tip.title: Bring a layer for tonight
tip.body: Today is pleasant at about 73F, but north wind gusts can reach 30 mph, and it drops to around 54F after dark. If you head out after Spanish, a light jacket will make the evening much more comfortable, and Sunday stays similar at about 71F and sunny.

ottoman.summary: After the war, Article 22 of the League of Nations Covenant placed former Ottoman lands under mandates, and the April 1920 San Remo conference handed Syria and Lebanon to France and Mesopotamia and Palestine to Britain. French forces crushed Faisal's Arab government in Damascus at Maysalun in July 1920, and Britain then made Faisal king of Iraq in 1921 after a costly revolt. Promised tutelage toward self-government meant outside control in practice, and these new borders were contested from the very start.

surprise.title: A crisp, clear sky and a nearly half moon tonight
surprise.body: Yesterday's cold front cleared the air, and the forecast for tonight is clear with a low around 53F. The Moon is a waxing crescent, 41% lit, rising at 2:04 PM and riding highest in the southern sky at 7:06 PM, right after sunset at 7:04 PM. When Spanish wraps at 8:00 PM, step outside and it will still be well up in the south-southwest. It reaches first quarter tomorrow at 12:12 PM, which in Spanish is cuarto creciente, and tonight's phase is luna creciente, so it doubles as two words for today's study.
